Marissa — thanks for the head’s up. Quick read: Acme’s ask (800–1.2k rps sustained @ ~1k tokens, p95 <= 150ms) is challenging but achievable with Dedicated if we configure the right instance mix and batching rules. High-level notes:
- Recommend reserved Dedicated pool with GPU instances sized for long contexts (we typically recommend 2x headroom for sustained traffic; plan for 1.6k rps capacity initially).
- For p95 <= 150ms at 1k tokens, we should disable aggressive batching for latency-sensitive routes and rely on prefix caching + request-level KV caching.
- Autoscale/fallback: suggest configuring a burst pool and a fallback model variant (quantized) if latency spikes under load.

I can be on the call. I’m available Fri 2/13 at 10:00am PST but suggest we block 60 minutes to cover traffic validation and rollout/SLAs. If Sophie is tight, we can do 45.

Questions to prep before the call (I'll ask during demo too):
1) Expected concurrent open sessions and average tokens per request (you noted ~1k tokens avg — can Acme provide a few representative prompts/traces?)
2) Any hard latency SLOs beyond p95 target (p50/p99 requirements)?

If you want, I’ll prepare a short capacity matrix and a latency chart from our perf runs to share.

– Dev Patel
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
